free_tier.stated: The Free plan costs nothing and needs no card: 1 live share at a time with a random name, shares of up to 2 hours, 1 uploaded site kept 7 days, and 1 GB of data a month.

egress.terms: 1 GB of data a month; ingress: http-only

interface_detail: run ouicu share 3000 beside your app
tooling: the ouicu CLI, plus an MCP server and SDK under MIT; the CLI and the service are closed
chaining: nothing to chain: HTTP-only and 1 GB a month, so it cannot carry UDP and cannot reach the volume bar
binding_note: 1 GB a month is short of 1 TiB by about three orders of magnitude, so the volume quota fails first; the 2-hour session cap is the second failure and has no vocabulary kind

identity_cost.detail: an Account page exists and ouicu whoami is documented, and the free plan is stated to need no card; the signup mechanism itself was not observed, so email is inferred from the absence of any phone or card requirement

reliability_note: the page states a live share stops while the laptop sleeps or is off and returns at the same address on reconnect; no ban or throttle is documented
confidence_note: the quota and the session length are documented on the vendor's own plans page; registration is inferred from an Account page and a whoami command, without an observed signup, so the record sits one rung below documented

evidence.proved: free plan needs no card, 1 live share at a time, 2-hour shares, 1 GB of data a month
per-plan table: 2-hour share limit on Free, no limit on Hobby and Pro, and an Account page
its own table lists protocols as HTTP and WebSockets, web pages only

notes: surfaced by because ouicu.com/compare is itself one of the twenty registry sources and the author discloses that he sells ouicu; there is no kind in the constraint vocabulary for a 2-hour session cap, so it is recorded here unclassified

extras.wg_detail: its own comparison table states the protocol as HTTP and WebSockets, web pages only; no WireGuard endpoint or raw TCP/UDP path is offered
extras.transit_note: ouicu's own relay carries the bytes
